column2: ENGLISH

The sores came first, then the rash. The surgeon would not meet my eyes when he named it: the Kruts, the pox of the bawdy-house, a gift every province of the Old World blames on its neighbours. It will fade and return for years, and some say it rots the mind in the end.
Curse every one of them!
The sores have healed and the rash has gone. The physician says the Kruts has burnt itself out, though he crossed himself as he said it, as if it might hear him.
May it never come back.

A patch of skin on my hand has gone numb and pale, and now there is another on my face. The servants whisper that it is the curse of the grey sickness, and already some of them will not touch the cup I drink from. Lepers are cast out of every city in the Old World. Will they cast out a [Root.GetLordLady]?
Unclean... I am unclean.

A sister of Shallya came to court with her salves and prayers, and asked only a gift for her temple's hospice. The grey patches have faded, the feeling has come back to my fingers, and the servants no longer flinch when I pass.
Mercy of Shallya, and well worth the gold.

The walls breathe. The candle flames lean towards me as I pass, and the portraits follow me with their eyes. When I told my steward, he laughed nervously and then stopped laughing. Something in my head has come loose, and I do not want to put it back.

They are all watching me. The servants, the guards, the birds on the sill. I have started counting the steps between my bed and the door every night, in case one of them has moved. One night, one will have.
The fever has broken, but something else broke with it. I still hear the voices I heard when I burned, and they still make sense to me. Nobody else seems to hear them.
I prayed until my knees bled, and at last the gods answered. They answer all the time now, at table, in council, in my sleep, and they do not always agree with one another.
I have been counting the stones of this cell. Every day there is a different number. The rats have names now, and opinions, and I have started taking their advice.

I have been asleep for a long time. I dreamt of a tower of glass and a sea of green fire, and when I woke I found that I had brought something back with me. The physicians are delighted that I can speak again. They are less delighted with what I say.
Everything is so clear now.
Let them watch. I will be watching back.
The voices are kind to me.
The gods have chosen me to listen.
Yes, Squeaker, I hear you.
I am awake. Are you?
This morning I woke and the walls were only walls. The candle flames stood straight. I feel a little foolish, and very tired, and more like myself than I have in a long time.
Let us never speak of it.

There is something else in my head with me. It speaks in my voice when I am not paying attention, and some mornings my hands are dirty with things I do not remember touching. The priests mutter about daemons and the Ruinous Powers, and keep their distance.
A djinn has crept into me through some careless word or broken oath. I feel it coil behind my eyes like smoke in a lamp, and sometimes, when I speak, the voice is not quite mine.
Get out of me!
Begone, spirit of the desert!

The priests prayed over me for three days and three nights, with holy water and prayers to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName]. On the third night the thing inside me screamed, and then it was gone. My soul is my own again.
The holy men burned incense and recited the old verses until the djinn could bear it no longer. It left me in a gust of hot wind that blew out every lamp in the room.
My will held, and in the end the spirit found it had no grip on my body or my soul. It has let go, and I am alone in my own head again.
Praise [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], I am free!
I am free!
There is always another petition, another dispute, another letter that cannot wait. I lie awake running over the day's business, and when I sleep I dream of ledgers. My hands shake when I hold a cup.
If only there were more hours in the day.
For the first time in months I slept through the night. The letters will keep. The world did not end while I rested.
I can breathe again.

I find myself lying in bed all day, the act of getting up almost as difficult as that of ruling. Food tastes bland, and my time spent with friends does not bring the joy it once did. I do not really understand why, but I hate my life.
What is the point of any of it?
This morning the sun came through the shutters and I found that I wanted to get up and see it. The grey weight that sat on my chest for so long has lifted.
Life is worth living after all.
My head aches, my bones ache, and I cannot keep food down. The physician has bled me twice and prescribed rest and broth. I hope Morr is not counting the days.
To bed, then.
The fever has broken. I am weak as a newborn foal, but I can stand, and the broth tastes of something again.
I am on the mend.
[Root.GetFirstName], once so pale and frail that the priests of Morr were kept waiting by the door, now runs about the courtyard chasing the hounds. The child has outgrown the sickness.
Look at [Root.GetHerHim] run!
The illness has gone to my chest. Every breath rattles and burns, and I cough until I taste blood. The physician speaks of the Rattlelung in a low voice.
Every breath is a battle.
The rattle in my chest has gone quiet. I can climb the tower stairs again without stopping to cough.
I can breathe freely again.
There is a burning when I make water, and blisters in places I would rather not show the physician. That last tryst was sweeter than it was wise.
Curses!
The wound has knitted closed at last. It has left a scar, an ugly one, but it no longer weeps or aches when it rains.
Another scar for the collection.
My wound has turned angry and red, and it smells of rot under the bandages. The surgeon frowns, and has started talking about the saw.
Fetch the surgeon.

My knees ache in the morning and my hands shake at the quill. The stairs to the hall are steeper than they used to be, and the faces of my courtiers have grown blurred. The years have caught up with me.
Where did the time go?

I can no longer tell my chamberlain from my grandchildren, and I have forgotten the names of half my vassals. The servants feed me with a spoon and speak about me as though I am not in the room. Perhaps I am not.
Who are you people?
The Weevil Cough that ate at my lungs for so long has finally let go. I am thin as a rake, but I am alive.
I have cheated Morr.
The Ochre Pox has passed. For weeks I burned and raved, and now I can hardly remember any of it.
I have cheated Morr.
The Red Pox has run its course. The rash is fading and my mind is clear again.
I have cheated Morr.
The plague doctor in his beaked mask says the buboes of the Black Plague have drained and the worst is past. Grandfather Nurgle has looked elsewhere this time.
Not this time, Plague Lord.
The Green Pox has run its course. The spots are gone and I can bear the light again.
I have cheated Morr.
The Ghoulpox has burnt itself out. My face will carry the marks for the rest of my life, but I still have a life.
I have cheated Morr.

The thing inside me has gone quiet, and in its place I hear a voice, warm and patient and full of light. It knows my name and every sin I have committed, and it forgives them. It can only be [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], come to guide me at last.
My god speaks to me!
The voice spoke to me during the night. It told me that the poor of my lands go hungry while my coffers are full, and that this displeases it.
Give alms to the poor.
The voice told me that my body is soft and my soul softer, and that I should wear a shirt of coarse hair beneath my robes as penance. My courtiers find it hard to keep a straight face when I scratch.
I will bear it gladly.

Last night a comet with two tails crossed the sky, burning blue and gold. The voice tells me it is a sign meant for me alone, and that greater things are coming. Strange, though: the second tail changed colour every time I looked at it.
I am chosen.
The voice told me that lust is a door through which darkness walks. It showed me all the faces I have desired, and asked me what any of them gave me.
I will put my lust aside.
The voice tells me that the body is a temple and should not be offered to just anyone.
I will lead a chaste life.
The voice told me that while I stuff myself, others starve, and that my belly is a monument to my weakness.
I will push the plate away.
The voice tells me to eat only what I need and to drink only water.
Bread and water it is.
The voice asked me what I will take with me to the halls of Morr. I counted my gold, and could not answer.
Gold is only dust.
The voice tells me that what I have was given to me so that I might give it to others.
Open the coffers.
The voice woke me before dawn and would not let me sleep again. It says there is work to do, and that the idle are easy prey for the Dark Gods.
I am up, I am up!
The voice tells me that every idle hour is stolen from the gods.
To work, then.
The voice asked me why I covet what others have, when the gods have already given me so much.
Let them have what is theirs.
The voice tells me to be gentle with others, for every one of them carries burdens I cannot see.
I will be kind.
The voice told me that my anger is a fire that will burn down my own house in the end.
I will master my temper.
The voice tells me that the gods work slowly, and that those who would serve them must learn to wait.
I can wait.
The voice showed me my own pride, and it was hideous.
I am nothing before the gods.
The voice tells me to kneel, and to remember that even a [Root.GetLordLady] is dust before the gods.
I kneel.

The voice has told me the truth at last: the priests have twisted the faith for their own ends, and their holy books are full of lies. Only I know what the gods truly want. It is a great relief to finally understand.
The priests have lied to us all!
The voice speaks to me of war now: where the enemy will march, where the ground is soft, where a flank lies open. So far it has never been wrong.
Lead on, and I will follow.
I asked the voice where the enemy would strike next, and it only laughed. It has said nothing about war since.
Speak to me!

The voice has given me a new tongue. The words pour out of me in council and at table, beautiful and strange, and nobody understands a single one. The envoys have started bringing scribes. The scribes have started bringing priests.
Ka'thrai! Ishtek-zhar!
This morning I asked for bread, and got bread. I can speak plainly again.
Words, at last.

The thing inside me has started to talk. Its voice is sweet as honey and old as the Realm of Chaos, and it tells me that the gods of my fathers are weak, and that the Dark Gods reward those who listen.
I am listening.
The voice is thirsty. It whispers of the prisoners in my dungeon and of how loudly they would scream. The Blood God, it says, does not care whose blood flows, only that it flows.
Bring the knives.
The voice laughs every time I show mercy. Mercy, it says, is how the weak ask the strong to stay weak.
No more mercy.
The voice whispers secrets to me: who is plotting with whom, who is bedding whose wife, who owes money to whom. The Changer of Ways delights in knowing things. So, it turns out, do I.
Tell me more.
The voice mocks my chastity. Why deny myself what so many would gladly give? The Prince of Pleasure, it says, would never ask me to.
Why indeed?
The voice fills my nights with visions of bodies and perfume and silk, and I wake aching with longing.
Yes...
The voice asks me how long I mean to wait while my enemies laugh at me. Patience, it says, is only cowardice in a robe.
No more waiting.
The voice stokes my anger like a smith works a forge. Every slight burns hotter, and I have started to enjoy the heat.
Blood for the Blood God!
The voice asks me why I bow to lesser beings. I am better than all of them, and it is time they knew it.
I deserve more.
The voice tells me I am perfect, the most beautiful and gifted soul in the Old World. I do not see why I should disagree.
I am perfect.
The voice laughs at my plain meals and watered wine. Grandfather Nurgle, it says, loves a full belly and a full cup.
Pour another.
The voice is always hungry, and now so am I. I eat at every meal as if it were my last, and then I eat again.
More!
The voice counts every coin I give away, and asks what the beggars ever did for me.
No more alms.
The voice shows me what gold can buy: loyalty, fear, pleasure, power. I want all of it.
Mine. All mine.
The voice shows me how everyone I have helped laughs at me behind my back. Kindness, it says, is just a weakness others feed on.
Never again.
The voice shows me everything that others have and I do not. Why should they have it, and not me?
Why them?
The voice asks me why I work so hard, when every labour rots in the end and every castle falls. Grandfather Nurgle, it says, is patient.
Why bother at all?
The voice lulls me to sleep in the middle of the day. My petitions pile up, and I find I do not care.
Tomorrow. Maybe.
The voice purrs whenever my eyes linger on a handsome face, whoever it belongs to. Why, it asks, should I deny myself half the world's delights? Every desire is a gift to the Dark Prince.
Why indeed?
I have had a marvellous idea for a new law, one that will set the realm right at last. My chancellor has gone very pale, but then he always looks like that.
Turnips are sacred, and must be honoured.
Breeches are forbidden throughout the realm!
Every subject shall dig a hole, for safety.
Every subject must strike their neighbour once a day.
The Turnip Law
The Breeches Law
The Hole Law
The Neighbour Law

A herald has brought word of a new law from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. From now on all turnips are sacred, must be greeted with a bow, and may not be eaten without a priest present. Peasants caught mashing them face the stocks.

A herald has brought word of a new law from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. The wearing of breeches is forbidden throughout the realm, on pain of a fine. The herald himself is wearing a long cloak and looks deeply uncomfortable.
A herald has brought word of a new law from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Every subject must dig a hole in their garden, at least three feet deep, 'for safety'. No one has been told what it is for.
A herald has brought word of a new law from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Every subject must now strike their neighbour once a day, 'to keep them honest'. There have already been riots in the market.
I will pretend I never received this.
I will pretend I never received this.
I will pretend I never received this.
I will pretend I never received this.

My herald reports that the turnip law has been received with great wonder. Turnips are greeted with a bow from the Reik to the borders. Some of my vassals have sent letters that I did not bother to read.
My herald reports that the breeches law is being obeyed. The markets are full of bare legs, and the tailors are rich. Some of my vassals have sent letters that I did not bother to read.

My herald reports that the hole law is being obeyed with great energy. The realm is full of holes, and several tax collectors have fallen into them. Some of my vassals have sent letters that I did not bother to read.
My herald reports that the neighbour law is being obeyed. Everyone in the realm is honest now, and most of them are bruised. Some of my vassals have sent letters that I did not bother to read.
Splendid.
The Turnip Law is proclaimed.
The Breeches Law is proclaimed.
The Hole Law is proclaimed.
The Neighbour Law is proclaimed.
I found a gopher in the garden today. It has very dignified whiskers and an excellent sense of decorum, and I have made it my personal maid. The other maids are jealous, of course.
Good gopher.
Mannslieb is full tonight, and Morrslieb lurks low behind it. I climbed to the battlements to greet them both, and I howled until the guards came running. They did not understand. The moons did.

Morrslieb hangs full and green over the land tonight, and it sings to me. I climbed to the battlements and howled back, and the green moon answered in a voice only I could hear. I have not stopped laughing since.
Awoooooo!
My chancellor is a dullard who brings me nothing but bad news. My horse, on the other hand, never complains, never argues and has an excellent mind for figures. I have made my decision.
Make way for the new chancellor!

The [From.GetTitle] has dismissed me from the council. That is bad enough, but I have just learned who will take my seat: [From.GetHerHis] horse. It has been given my chain of office, and it is already eating my papers.
A horse. A horse!
A horse now sits on the council.

There is something scratching inside the walls of my bedchamber. At night I hear it whisper, squeaking voices that speak of a Horned One and a great city beneath the earth. Everyone knows the ratmen are a story told to frighten children. Still, I cannot sleep, and when I do I dream of the grey sea.
I must find out where the dreams lead.
Call the ratcatcher and be done with it.
At the bottom of the old castle well there is a light, faint and green, that pulses like a heartbeat. When I lean over the edge I can hear the sea, though the coast is many leagues away.
Lower me down.
Seal the well with stone.

My men broke into one of the old barrows in the hills, the ones the peasants say belong to the kings before Sigmar. The dead king inside had a mouth full of wet sand and seaweed, and his finger pointed north.
It is calling me. I will go.
Fill it in and salt the earth.

I have noticed that the cats of the castle sit on the walls every evening and stare towards the sea, all of them, without blinking. They know something. From today, no cat may be harmed in my lands, on pain of death.
The cats are watching. I must protect them.
They are only cats.

The dreams have led me north, to a grey fishing village on the shore of the Sea of Claws. The villagers are pale and their eyes are large and wet, and none of them seems to blink. They are very polite, and they have offered me a bed for the night.
I will stay.
The dreams lead to the coast.
At low tide the villagers gathered on the shore and began to chant in a language older than Reikspiel. To my surprise I knew the words, and joined in.
I know these words...
The villagers hold a rite on the shore.

The sea drew back, far further than any tide, and something rose out of the grey water. It was larger than a war galley, with too many eyes and a crown of writhing limbs, and the villagers knelt and sang to it. It is calling me by name.
Walk into the sea to meet it.
RUN!
Something rises from the sea.
I ran to the jetty, leapt into a fishing longboat and seized a whaler's harpoon. The thing turned all of its eyes on me. I rowed straight at it.
For the Old World!
You face the thing from the deep.

I woke on the beach at dawn, soaked to the bone. The village is empty, the longboat is gone, and there is no sign of anything in the grey water. Yet in my hand is a tooth as long as my forearm, and my clothes reek of something that never lived on land.
It was a fever dream, nothing more.
I slew it. I know I did.
You wake on the shore.

A loud sneeze interrupts [Root.GetMyMarshalName] [Root.job_marshal.GetTitledFirstName]'s speech on the importance of camp hygiene. 'I am sorry, my [Root.GetLordLady],' mutters [Root.job_spymaster.GetTitledFirstName], the [Root.GetSpymasterName], casting a quick glance at the cat on my lap. 'If you could only leave the creature out of our meetings, this would not happen again, I swear.'
How dare you blame little innocent Mittens?!
Perhaps you are right, [Root.job_spymaster.GetFirstName]. The council is no place for a cat.

I am awoken by a soft pat on my cheek. 'Oh, Mittens. Are you having trouble falling asleep?' She jumps down from my bed and starts pawing at the door. 'Let's go to the kitchen and get you some warm milk.' But as I close my bedroom door behind me, Mittens heads in the opposite direction.
Follow Mittens down the dark corridor.
Go to the kitchen, she is sure to follow.

As I round a corner, I spot Mittens' fluffy tail as she squeezes through the chamber door of my [Root.GetSpymasterName], [Root.job_spymaster.GetFullName]! I enter, finding Mittens curled up on [Root.job_spymaster.GetHerHis] chest, licking [Root.job_spymaster.GetHerHis] face, but [Root.job_spymaster.GetFirstName] does not react. The [Root.job_spymaster.GetManWoman] before me is completely still, not even breathing, and [Root.job_spymaster.GetHerHis] face is strangely swollen...
You have discovered a murder, Mittens! Clever kitty!

Apparently, it was not bad enough when that stupid animal glared at us from the safety of [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]'s lap. Now it has its own chair, and a seat on the council, to boot! The [FromFrom.GetTitle] has informed us that the former [FromFrom.GetSpymasterName] was poisoned, but a servant who helped move the body insists that the [FromFrom.GetSpymasterName] was suffocated...
Is anyone on the council safe? This is a catastrophe!

[From.GetSheHeCap] is so cute and fluffy, what would life even be like if I were to lose [From.GetHerHim]? I am not sure I could go on... I must do something about this and protect my beloved cat [From.GetBestName].
[From.GetSheHeCap] must lap up some of my immortal blood for protection.
Only I shall have this great power!
Twin-Tailed Omen
This character has seen a comet with two tails and believes it was a sign sent to them alone.
Voice of Battle
A voice in this character's head gives uncannily good advice on matters of war.
Speaking in Tongues
This character babbles in a tongue no one understands, and swears it is holy.
Slayer of the Thing Beneath
This character swears they slew a horror from the depths of the Sea of Claws, and has the tooth to prove it.
Tooth of the Thing Beneath
A tooth as long as a forearm, stained green and smelling of the deep sea. Its owner swears they pulled it from a horror that rose out of the Sea of Claws.
Has the Black Plague
This character has the Black Plague, the rat-borne pestilence that once emptied whole provinces of the Empire.
Has Lustrian Fever
This character burns with a fever brought back from the jungles of Lustria, against which the physicians of the Old World have no remedy.

There is an old brass lamp in my treasury, taken from some Arabyan tomb long ago. At night it whispers. It speaks of a city beneath the dunes of the Great Desert, a city that sings, and it says the song is for me.
I will listen.
Melt the cursed thing down.

The well in my courtyard has started to bring up black sand, fine as flour and warm to the touch. Every night since, the temple bell has rung by itself, always thirteen times. When I hold the sand to my ear I hear singing.
Dig deeper.
Fill in the well.

I bought a map from a scholar of Remas, drawn in a tongue no one alive can read. It shows a city deep in the Great Desert, south of the Spice Road. No other map has it, and the scholar drowned in his own fountain the day after he sold it to me.
Follow the map.
Burn the map.
The statue of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] in my temple has begun to weep, but not tears. Sand runs from its eyes, black sand, a little more each day, always pooling towards the south.
It is a warning, and a summons.
Have it cleaned and say nothing.
The song leads into the desert.
I have joined a spice caravan heading south into the Great Desert. The caravan master thinks I am a pilgrim. At night, when the camels are hobbled, I can hear the dunes singing, and nobody else can.
Ride on.
The caravan finds an unknown oasis.

The caravan found an oasis that the caravan master swears was not there last year. Veiled people live there, who never show their faces, and at dusk they gathered by the water and sang the song from my dreams. I found I knew every word.
Sing with them.
The dunes part.

At midnight the dunes slid away like water, and a city of black glass rose out of the sand, towers within towers, all of them singing. The veiled people knelt. In the heart of the city, something opened an eye as large as a gate, and looked at me.
Walk into the city.
RUN!
You flee into the storm.
I stole a camel and rode into the desert as a sandstorm rose behind me. The song became a scream. Something vast was moving under the sand, following me.
Faster!
You wake at a well.

I woke beside a well at the edge of the desert, my lips cracked and my camel gone. The caravan is gone and the oasis cannot be found. Yet I hold a shard of black glass in my hand, and when the wind blows from the south, it hums.
It was the sun and the thirst, nothing more.
I broke its heart. That is why it screamed.

The stars over Lustria are not the stars of home. I have been watching them every night, and I have realized that they move in patterns, and that the patterns are writing. Someone wrote them. Someone is still writing.
I must learn to read them.
I will stop looking up.

Every night a skink leaves a carved stone at the gate of the colony and slips back into the jungle. The guards have collected twelve of them. Every one is carved with my face, and on each one I am a little older.
Keep the stones. Count them.
Shoot the next skink that comes.

The gold we took from the temple-city lies in my strongroom, and it whispers. It speaks in a language of clicks and hisses that I am beginning to understand. It wants to go home, and it wants me to carry it.
Then I will take it home.
Melt it into coin.
In the grip of a jungle fever I dreamt of a great, bloated sage on a golden throne, older than the world, whose eyes were closed. He spoke to me without opening his mouth. He already knew my name.
He is calling me.
It is only the fever talking.
The dreams lead into the jungle.
I have hired porters and a few mercenaries who ask no questions, and we are cutting our way into the jungle. I know the way without a map. The porters have noticed.
Onward.
The expedition finds a temple-city.
The jungle fell silent around a great step-pyramid, without a bird or an insect to be heard. Skinks watched us from every ledge and did not attack. On the stairs were glyphs, and I could read them.
Read the glyphs.
Something waits inside.

At the heart of the temple a slann sat in a pool of starlight, its eyes closed. I understood then that it had been dreaming me, that my whole life had been a passing thought in its plan, and that it was about to wake.
Step into the light.
RUN!
You flee down the river.
I fled to the river and threw myself onto a raft. Behind me the jungle screamed back to life, and something vast moved under the brown water, keeping pace with me.
Row!
You wake in the colony.

I woke in my own bed in the colony, soaked in sweat. The porters swear we never left. But on my chest lies a plaque of beaten gold, covered in the script of the Old Ones, and I can still read every word.
It was the fever. It must have been.
I read it, and I remember.
Heartbreaker of the Singing City
This character claims to have broken the heart of a city of black glass beneath the Great Desert. Nobody else heard it scream.
Woke from the Slann's Dream
This character walked into a slann's dream and walked out again, and now reads the script of the Old Ones.
Shard of Black Glass
A shard of glass as black as a moonless night, from a city that sings beneath the Great Desert. It hums when the wind blows from the south.
Plaque of the Dreaming Temple
A plaque of beaten gold covered in the script of the Old Ones, carried out of a slann's temple-city in Lustria. The lizardmen would very much like it back.
ENGLISH
What was that shadow? You could have sworn you heard someone whispering behind your back. Why would someone follow you in the first place?
A plot?

People suffer all the time, but why care? As long as you are alright, there's nothing to be sad about. In fact, how could you consider yourself well-being, if not by comparison with those who are not?
Their suffering makes me feel better.
All this stress plaguing your mind is just too much. You need something to calm yourself, anything!
Some herbs might help, maybe?

Incompetent narrow-minded fools might play safe with magic, but you know better by now: one cannot truly master the Winds without taking a few risks. This last experiment might really help you better understand the arcane.
Let's start now!
As you expected, the experiment was successful. Each day your mind opens more to the great secrets of the universe.
I must know more!
You spent an entire night of work for nothing: the secret of this spell still eludes you. All the time wasted for a failure is driving you mad.
I need to start again! I must know!
Collateral damage is inevitable when fighting for control over the great powers of the universe. You just hoped the fire wouldn't spread to yourself as well.
Aaargh!!
This is the last time you have to wake up with a damning headache without remembering what you did the previous night. Alcohol is poison and you shall not submit your brilliant mind to it ever again.
I've better things to think!

Nobody is truly ever evil, the more you think about it. All people have good reasons for their actions and those who are said to be wicked are just sad and lonely beings, who were probably abused when young. Why should you add to their misery by branding them as villains?
There is no evil.
You've always known to be special, but you are certain now that the Winds of Magic flow through you, granting you powers that mere mortals only dream of.
I'm a powerful mage!

Most people don't see it, but in the end isn't life one big joke? You can see it now, it might be you just have keener senses or maybe you're the protagonist of this farce. Why else would other people not see the hilarity in murder or the humour in misery?
Ah ah ah ah ah!

For some time now hardly anything has been able to trigger a response for you. As time passes by not only do you no longer feel any passion left for your loved ones nor hatred for your enemies, your very skin has started to lose any perception.
I feel... nothing.

Life is something miraculous, when you take one, you can feel all of the vibrant passions and dreams of a dying soul. It lasts but a moment, it's never enough to sate your thirst for death. And off you go, searching for the next target.
The blood calls...
People have always had to look up on you, they know you're better than them in every way and so do you. Are you even one of them, you wonder? Perhaps you are something more...
...more than a mortal!

You couldn't help it, it was such a beautiful scene... The body moves now, but soon your blade shall turn it into a motionless puppet and shall be able to watch as the soul passes away into the Realm beyond...
Soon...
